target_customer: High growth startups and scaleups that need commercial, corporate and employment legal work
problem: Fast growing companies wait days and pay hourly rates for routine contract review and negotiation.
business_model: AI native law firm with flat fee pricing per matter (about 500 dollars per contract review and negotiation on existing paper)

founders.name: Ryan Walker
founders.background_notes: YC page: former CTO of Casetext.

founders.name: J.P. Mohler
founders.background_notes: YC page: iOS and Android developer who represented startups and VCs for three years.

founders.name: Javed Qadrud-Din
founders.background_notes: YC page spells the name Qadruddin; led AI at Casetext.

competitors.name: Norm Law
competitors.what: AI native firm affiliated with Norm Ai
competitors.funding_then: affiliate Norm Ai reported a 120M Series C

competitors.name: Soxton
competitors.what: AI law firm focused on helping startups
competitors.traction_then: already focused on startups per Artificial Lawyer

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires reliable legal AI workflows plus a licensed attorney review process and a law firm structure; founders had built Casetext CoCounsel experience.

defensibility.rationale: Law firm licensing limits software only entrants, but several AI native firms launched in the same months.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Traditional firms and other AI native firms were moving in 2026; no takeover action found.

market_need_then: Startups complain about slow, expensive contract work; the company reports over 20 growth stage companies moved contracting to it after private preview (YC launch post).

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and speed focused, phrases such as Legal at AI Speed and The law firm you've been waiting for

branding.brand_signature: Three hour guaranteed contract turnaround at a flat price
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Artificial Lawyer, LawNext, MLex and Product Hunt (launched 2026-02-25).

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive name with a strong offer and trade press coverage, though the name is generic.

outcome_analysis: The firm is active and grew to about 40 people within its Winter 2026 batch. Founders with Casetext and Big Law backgrounds built credibility and the press reported an 11.5M combined seed and pre-seed raise within three months of launch. The main risk is competition from other AI native firms and traditional firms.
notes: Artificial Lawyer reports 11.5M as combined Seed and Pre-Seed, so the stage is recorded as other. MLex independently reports the 11.5M figure. CB Insights dates the seed 2026-03-25 and VCBacked says 2026-02; extra investors (Pioneer Fund, Spot VC) appear only on an aggregator and are not recorded. Stanford CodeX lists the company as no longer active, which conflicts with all other sources. Founded year is 2026 on the YC page but one summary says 2025.
